_comment: Tier-2 FALSIFICATION: pitfall (kratos.curved_mms #0) records that 'Kratos 10.4 on this host works ONLY under the system /usr/bin/python3 (Python 3.8)' and that 'the pip Kratos wheel inside the repo .venv is BROKEN: its shared libraries require GLIBC 2.32 which the OS libc does not provide'. THAT IS A PROPERTY OF THE 10.4.2 WHEEL, NOT OF THE HOST. Measured: on the same glibc-2.31 machine, KratosMultiphysics 10.4.3 in a Python 3.12 venv imports and runs — nothing in the 10.4.3 wheel needs a symbol above GLIBC_2.17, and its manylinux_2_28 tag is satisfied by glibc 2.31. This fixture asserts that it is itself running under a non-system, non-3.8 interpreter inside a venv, and that a real Kratos call works there, so it cannot pass by accident on the interpreter the claim prescribes. The operational advice in that entry — run generated scripts with /usr/bin/python3 — is therefore stale and costs a user the newer wheel. The fixture imports KratosMultiphysics at module scope; with Kratos absent the import raises, the process exits non-zero and the runner records a failure, never a pass.
